claim: Arl15 is an Arf-like small G protein.
source: Here, we report that active Arl15, an Arf-like small G protein, specifically binds to the MH2 domain of Smad4 and colocalizes with Smad4 at the endolysosome.
evidence: The abstract directly states that Arl15 is an Arf-like small G protein.

claim: Active Arl15 specifically binds to the MH2 domain of Smad4.
source: Here, we report that active Arl15, an Arf-like small G protein, specifically binds to the MH2 domain of Smad4 and colocalizes with Smad4 at the endolysosome.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Arl15 colocalizes with Smad4 at the endolysosome.

claim: The binding of Arl15 to Smad4 relieves the autoinhibition of Smad4.

claim: Smad4 autoinhibition is imposed by the intramolecular interaction between its MH1 and MH2 domains.

claim: Activated Smad4 interacts with phosphorylated receptor-regulated Smads to form the Smad-complex.

claim: Smad4 functions as an effector of Arl15.

claim: Depleting Arl15 does not significantly change the cellular level of phospho-Smad2/3 stimulated by the TGFβ1 treatment.
source: We first demonstrated that depleting Arl15 does not significantly change the cellular level of phospho-Smad2/3 stimulated by the TGFβ1 treatment (Figure 4h).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 4h.

claim: The depletion of Arl15 substantially reduced phospho-Smad2/3 immunoprecipitated by Smad4.
source: Importantly, consistent with our above overexpression studies, we found that the depletion of Arl15 substantially reduced phospho-Smad2/3 immunoprecipitated by Smad4 (Figure 4i), suggesting an essential role of Arl15 in the efficient assembly of the Smad-complex.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 4i.

claim: Arl15 has an essential role in the efficient assembly of the Smad-complex.
source: Importantly, consistent with our above overexpression studies, we found that the depletion of Arl15 substantially reduced phospho-Smad2/3 immunoprecipitated by Smad4 (Figure 4i), suggesting an essential role of Arl15 in the efficient assembly of the Smad-complex.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this as a suggestion based on the data.

claim: Arl15-GTP might promote the assembly of the Smad-complex by binding to and activating the Smad4-MH2 domain.
source: Collectively, our data showed that Arl15-GTP might promote the assembly of the Smad-complex by binding to and activating the Smad4-MH2 domain.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this as a conclusion based on the data.

claim: Arl15 did not localize to the nucleus under the TGFβ1 treatment.
source: In fluorescence imaging, we observed that Arl15 did not localize to the nucleus under the TGFβ1 treatment (Figure 5a).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 5a.

claim: The nuclear localization of phospho-Smad2/3 increased substantially under TGFβ1 treatment.
source: In contrast, the nuclear localization of phospho-Smad2/3 increased substantially (Figure 5a).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 5a.

claim: Arl15 was not detected in the nuclear fraction in starved or TGFβ1 stimulated control knockdown cells.
source: Consistent with our imaging, we did not detect Arl15 in the nuclear fraction in starved or TGFβ1 stimulated control knockdown cells (Figure 5b).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 5b.

claim: In control or Arl15 knockdown cells, nuclear fractions of phospho-Smad2/3 and Smad4 substantially increased under the TGFβ1 treatment compared to the starvation treatment.
source: However, in control or Arl15 knockdown cells, nuclear fractions of phospho-Smad2/3 and Smad4 substantially increased under the TGFβ1 treatment compared to the starvation treatment (Figure 5b).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 5b.

claim: When Arl15 was depleted, substantially less phospho-Smad2/3 and Smad4 were found in the nuclear fraction.
source: Notably, when Arl15 was depleted, substantially less phospho-Smad2/3 and Smad4 were found in the nuclear fraction (Figure 5b–d).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 5b–d.

claim: Arl15 is essential for the efficient assembly of the Smad-complex, which subsequently translocates to the nucleus.
source: The finding thus supports our hypothesis that Arl15 is essential for the efficient assembly of the Smad-complex, which subsequently translocates to the nucleus.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this as a hypothesis supported by the data.

claim: Smad4, but not Smad2-SE, substantially accelerated the GTP hydrolysis rate of Arl15.
source: We found that Arl15-WT alone displayed a weak GTP-hydrolysis activity and that the presence of Smad4, but not Smad2-SE, substantially accelerated the GTP hydrolysis rate of Arl15, demonstrating Smad4 as a potential GAP for Arl15 (Figure 5e).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 5e.

claim: The addition of Smad2-SE greatly enhanced the GAP activity of Smad4 toward Arl15.
source: Interestingly, the addition of Smad2-SE greatly enhanced the GAP activity of Smad4 toward Arl15.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 5e.

claim: AL mutation abolished the GTP hydrolysis activity of Arl15 in all cases.
source: As expected for a small G protein, we observed that AL mutation abolished the GTP hydrolysis activity of Arl15 in all cases — either alone or with the addition of Smad4 or Smad2-SE, retrospectively confirming AL as the GTPase-defective mutation.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 5e.

claim: The GAP activity of Smad4 toward Arl15 was mapped to the Smad4-MH2 domain.
source: Using purified domains of Smad4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1b), we mapped the GAP activity to the Smad4-MH2 domain (Figure 5f).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 5f and Figure 5—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The extension of the MH2 domain to include the linker region further increased the GAP activity.
source: The extension of the MH2 domain to include the linker region further increased the GAP activity (Figure 5f).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 5f.

claim: After the assembly of the Smad-complex, Smad4 might have an enhanced GAP activity and consequently inactivate Arl15 and dissociate the latter from the complex.
source: In summary, our data suggest that, after the assembly of the Smad-complex, Smad4 might have an enhanced GAP activity and consequently inactivate Arl15 and dissociate the latter from the complex.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this as a suggestion based on the data.

claim: Arl15-AL reduced the percentage of nuclear Smad4 and phospho-Smad2/3 compared to the control.
source: Our nuclear fractionation assay demonstrates that Arl15-AL reduced the percentage of nuclear Smad4 and phospho-Smad2/3 compared to the control (Figure 5g–i).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 5g–i.

claim: When bound, Arl15 seems to inhibit the nuclear translocation of the Smad-complex.
source: Therefore, when bound, Arl15 seems to inhibit the nuclear translocation of the Smad-complex.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this as a conclusion based on the data.

claim: The Smad-complex must inactivate and dissociate the bound Arl15 for efficient nuclear translocation.
source: The Smad-complex must inactivate and dissociate the bound Arl15 for efficient nuclear translocation.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this as a conclusion based on the data.

claim: Overexpression of Arl15-WT or AL, but not TN, was sufficient to stimulate the transcription of SBE ×4 luc to ≥2 fold that of the control under serum-starvation.
source: We found that when HeLa cells were treated with the serum-free medium (serum-starvation or hereafter referred to as starvation), overexpression of Arl15-WT or AL, but not TN, was sufficient to stimulate the transcription of SBE ×4 luc to ≥2 fold that of the control (Figure 6a).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 6a.

claim: The stimulation by Arl15-AL was abolished by SB431542, a small molecule inhibitor of TGFβ type I receptor kinase activity.
source: The stimulation was abolished by SB431542 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a), a small molecule inhibitor of TGFβ type I receptor kinase activity (Laping et al., 2002).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 6—figure supplement 1a and citing Laping et al., 2002.

claim: Overexpression of Arl15-WT or AL, but not TN, also stimulated the transcription of BRE-luc.
source: Similarly, we found that overexpression of Arl15-WT or AL, but not TN, also stimulated the transcription of BRE-luc (Figure 6—figure supplement 1b), a luciferase reporter for assaying the BMP R-Smad-dependent transcription or BMP signaling (Korchynskyi and ten Dijke, 2002).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 6—figure supplement 1b and citing Korchynskyi and ten Dijke, 2002.

claim: When endogenous Arl15 was depleted by RNAi, TGFβ1 or BMP2-induced reporter transcription was attenuated to less than half of the control.
source: On the other hand, when endogenous Arl15 was depleted by RNAi (Figure 6—figure supplement 1c), TGFβ1 or BMP2-induced reporter transcription was attenuated to less than half of the control, and the autocrine stimulated transcription also decreased under starvation (Figure 6b; Figure 6—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 6b, Figure 6—figure supplement 1c, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1d.

claim: Arl15 is a positive and essential regulator for the complete activity of TGFβ and BMP signaling pathways.
source: Hence, our data imply that Arl15 is a positive and essential regulator for the complete activity of TGFβ and BMP signaling pathways.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this as an implication from the data.

claim: Arl15 knockdown did not substantially affect the ER-to-Golgi trafficking.
source: Using ManII (a Golgi transmembrane glycosidase) and TNFα (a PM-targeted transmembrane protein) RUSH reporters (Boncompain et al., 2012), we found that Arl15 knockdown did not substantially affect the ER-to-Golgi (Figure 6—figure supplement 1e and f) and the subsequent Golgi-to-PM trafficking (Figure 6—figure supplement 1g and h).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 6—figure supplement 1e and f and citing Boncompain et al., 2012.

claim: Arl15 knockdown did not substantially affect the Golgi-to-PM trafficking.
source: Using ManII (a Golgi transmembrane glycosidase) and TNFα (a PM-targeted transmembrane protein) RUSH reporters (Boncompain et al., 2012), we found that Arl15 knockdown did not substantially affect the ER-to-Golgi (Figure 6—figure supplement 1e and f) and the subsequent Golgi-to-PM trafficking (Figure 6—figure supplement 1g and h).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 6—figure supplement 1g and h and citing Boncompain et al., 2012.

claim: TGFβ1-stimulated phosphorylation of Smad2/3 normally occurred upon knockdown of Arl15.
source: Next, we observed that TGFβ1-stimulated phosphorylation of Smad2/3 normally occurred upon knockdown of Arl15 (Figure 1c, Figure 4h, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1i).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 1c, Figure 4h, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1i.

claim: Arl15 is probably not required for steps leading to phosphorylation of Smad2/3, such as trafficking and maintenance of TGFβ1 receptors and Smad2/3.
source: Therefore, Arl15 is probably not required for steps leading to phosphorylation of Smad2/3, such as trafficking and maintenance of TGFβ1 receptors and Smad2/3.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this as a conclusion based on the data.

claim: Arl15 regulates the TGFβ family signaling by promoting the assembly of the Smad-complex.
source: In summary, our data argue against the hypothesis that Arl15 indirectly regulates the TGFβ family signaling by intracellular trafficking. Instead, they support a model in which Arl15 regulates the TGFβ family signaling by promoting the assembly of the Smad-complex.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this as a conclusion based on the data.

claim: Overexpression of Arl15-AL, but not TN and empty vector control, was sufficient to upregulate the transcription of N-cadherin, ID1, Snail1, p27kip1, p21cip1, Fibronectin, and α-SMA in serum-starved MCF7 cells.
source: In serum-starved MCF7 cells, overexpression of Arl15-AL, but not TN and empty vector control, was sufficient to upregulate the transcription of N-cadherin, ID1, Snail1, p27kip1, p21cip1, Fibronectin, and α-SMA, and downregulate the transcription of E-cadherin and c-Myc (Figure 6c and d).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 6c and d.

claim: Overexpression of Arl15-AL downregulated the transcription of E-cadherin and c-Myc in serum-starved MCF7 cells.
source: In serum-starved MCF7 cells, overexpression of Arl15-AL, but not TN and empty vector control, was sufficient to upregulate the transcription of N-cadherin, ID1, Snail1, p27kip1, p21cip1, Fibronectin, and α-SMA, and downregulate the transcription of E-cadherin and c-Myc (Figure 6c and d).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 6c and d.

claim: Under TGFβ1 treatment, depletion of Arl15 in MCF7 cells reversed the transcriptional trend of genes compared to control knockdown.
source: On the other hand, under TGFβ1 treatment, depletion of Arl15 in MCF7 cells reversed the transcriptional trend of the above genes compared to control knockdown, that is, those that were upregulated by Arl15-AL overexpression (e.g., N-cadherin, ID1, Snail1, p27kip1, and p21cip1) became downregulated, and vice versa (e.g. E-cadherin and c-Myc) (Figure 6e).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 6e.

claim: A similar result was obtained when Arl15 was depleted in the MDA-MB-231 cell line.
source: A similar result was obtained when Arl15 was depleted in the MDA-MB-231 cell line, representing highly metastatic breast cancer cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1j and k).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 6—figure supplement 1j and k.

claim: The activity of Arl15 correlates with a gene transcription profile characteristic of the TGFβ-induced cytostasis and EMT in cancer cells.
source: Therefore, our observation correlates the activity of Arl15 with a gene transcription profile characteristic of the TGFβ-induced cytostasis and EMT in cancer cells.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this as a conclusion based on the data.

claim: Overexpression of Arl15-AL slightly reduced the transcription of SBE ×4 luc in HeLa cells under TGFβ1 treatment.
source: Surprisingly, we found that overexpression of Arl15-AL slightly reduced the transcription of SBE ×4 luc in HeLa cells under TGFβ1 treatment (Figure 6—figure supplement 1l).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 6—figure supplement 1l.

claim: Arl15-AL might have two opposing effects on the Smad-complex – promoting its assembly and inhibiting its nuclear translocation.
source: Therefore, we propose that Arl15-AL might have two opposing effects on the Smad-complex – promoting its assembly and inhibiting its nuclear translocation.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this as a proposal based on the data.

claim: The migration and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells were significantly reduced upon depletion of Arl15.
source: By wound healing and collagen gel invasion assays, we observed that the migration and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells were significantly reduced upon depletion of Arl15 (Figure 7a–d).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 7a–d.

claim: Arl15 is required for the efficient in vitro migration and invasion of cancerous cells.
source: Efficient in vitro migration and invasion of cancerous cells require Arl15
evidence: This is stated in the section heading and supported by data in Figure 7a–d.

claim: Cancer missense mutations R90L, R95C, and Y96F in the switch-II region of Arl15 specifically attenuated the Arl15-Smad4 interaction.
source: We found that the following single point mutations in the switch-II region specifically attenuated the Arl15-Smad4 interaction: R90L, R95C, and Y96F, as demonstrated in our pull-down assays (Figure 7e).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 7e.

claim: Cancer missense mutations R90L, R95C, and Y96F in Arl15 substantially reduced the stimulation of Arl15-AL in the transcription of SBE ×4 luc under starvation.
source: These mutations also substantially reduced the stimulation of Arl15-AL in the transcription of SBE ×4 luc under starvation (Figure 7f).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 7f.

claim: Cancer patients can have genetic mutations or alterations that compromise the Arl15-Smad4 interaction.
source: Combined with cancer mutations in the Smad4-MH2 domain (Figure 1j and k), our data demonstrate that cancer patients can have genetic mutations or alterations that compromise the Arl15-Smad4 interaction and suggest that such genetic changes might contribute to tumorigenesis by down-regulating the TGFβ signaling pathway.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this, referring to Figure 1j and k.

claim: Genetic changes that compromise the Arl15-Smad4 interaction might contribute to tumorigenesis by down-regulating the TGFβ signaling pathway.
source: Combined with cancer mutations in the Smad4-MH2 domain (Figure 1j and k), our data demonstrate that cancer patients can have genetic mutations or alterations that compromise the Arl15-Smad4 interaction and suggest that such genetic changes might contribute to tumorigenesis by down-regulating the TGFβ signaling pathway.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this as a suggestion based on the data.

claim: Arl15 is the first small G protein reported to interact with Smads.
source: According to our knowledge, it is the first small G protein reported to interact with Smads.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this.

claim: Opening and activation of Smad4 is specifically aided by Arl15-GTP through direct binding to the MH2 domain of Smad4.
source: We discovered that opening and, hence, activation of Smad4 is specifically aided by Arl15-GTP through direct binding to the MH2 domain of Smad4.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this as a discovery from the study.

claim: Arl15 is a potential signaling integration node between a small G-protein activation cascade and the TGFβ family signaling.
source: Hence, our study reveals Arl15 as a potential signaling integration node between a small G-protein activation cascade and the TGFβ family signaling.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this as a conclusion from the study.

claim: The Smad-complex is an effector and a terminator for active Arl15.
source: Our model proposes that the Smad-complex is an effector and a terminator for active Arl15, which promotes the assembly of the Smad-complex in the first place.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this as part of the proposed model.

claim: Sar1 is an Arf-family small G protein that initiates the assembly of the COPII coat at the ER exit site.
source: Sar1 is an Arf-family small G protein that initiates the assembly of the COPII coat at the ER exit site.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this, citing prior literature.

claim: In Sec23-Sec24 heterodimer, Sec23 functions as both an effector and a GAP for Sar1.
source: In Sec23-Sec24 heterodimer, Sec23 functions as both an effector and a GAP for Sar1.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this, citing prior literature.

claim: Arl15 and Sar1 have Ala (at 86) and His (at 77) in their G3-motifs, respectively, in contrast to Gln of other Arf-family small G proteins.
source: We note that Arl15 and Sar1 have Ala (at 86) and His (at 77) in their G3-motifs, respectively, in contrast to Gln of other Arf-family small G proteins.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this.

claim: Conserved Gln in the G3-motif functions to facilitate the GTP hydrolysis by correctly positioning the water molecule.
source: Conserved Gln in the G3-motif functions to facilitate the GTP hydrolysis by correctly positioning the water molecule.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this.

claim: Termination of active Sar1 and Arl15 in vivo probably requires their effector-cum-GAPs.
source: Therefore, termination of active Sar1 and Arl15 in vivo probably requires their effector-cum-GAPs, which ensure the proper assembly of the COPII coat and the Smad-complex, respectively, before the complete dissociation of small G proteins.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this as a conclusion based on the data and comparison with Sar1.

claim: Arl15 might be a pro-metastatic factor.
source: Our observation that Arl15 is required for the efficient invasion and migration of malignant cancer cells suggests that it might be a pro-metastatic factor.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this as a suggestion based on the data.

claim: Arl15 might be a tumor suppressor.
source: However, the finding of mutations compromising the Arl15-Smad4 interaction in the cancer genomic database suggests that Al15 might be a tumor suppressor.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this as a suggestion based on the data.

claim: The TGFβ signaling pathway possesses a context-dependent dual-role in cancer progression.
source: It is well known that the TGFβ signaling pathway possesses a context-dependent dual-role in cancer progression (Massagué, 2008; Massagué, 2012).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this, citing references.

claim: In normal epithelia or pre-malignant cancers, the TGFβ signaling pathway exerts a cytostatic or tumor-suppressive effect to inhibit the proliferation of cells.
source: In normal epithelia or pre-malignant cancers, the TGFβ signaling pathway exerts a cytostatic or tumor-suppressive effect to inhibit the proliferation of cells.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this.

claim: In malignant or metastatic cancers, TGFβ signaling exerts a pro-metastatic effect to promote growth and invasion of cells.
source: On the other hand, in malignant or metastatic cancers, TGFβ signaling exerts a pro-metastatic effect to promote growth and invasion of cells.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this.

claim: Arl15 might play a similar dual-role in cancer progression like Smad4.
source: Therefore, we hypothesize that, like Smad4, Arl15 might play a similar dual-role in cancer progression.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this as a hypothesis.

claim: Arl15 also participates in the BMP signaling pathway.
source: Although our study mainly focused on the TGFβ signaling pathway, we observed that Arl15 promotes the assembly of the BMP Smad-complex (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), and it is essential for the full activity of BMP R-Smad-dependent transcription (Figure 6—figure supplement 1d). Therefore, our data indicate that Arl15 also participates in the BMP signaling pathway.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this, referring to Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1d.

claim: Competition between TGFβ and BMP pathways for Smad4 contributes to their antagonistic cellular effects.
source: It has been proposed that competition between TGFβ and BMP pathways for Smad4 contributes to their antagonistic cellular effects (Candia et al., 1997; Sartori et al., 2013; Yuan et al., 2018).
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this, citing references.

claim: Similar to Smad4, Arl15 might mediate antagonistic crosstalk between the TGFβ and BMP pathways.
source: Hence, we speculate that, similar to Smad4, Arl15 might mediate antagonistic crosstalk between the two pathways.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this as speculation.

claim: The findings raise the likelihood of ARL15 as the causative gene in metabolic diseases.
source: Consistent with the broad role of the TGFβ signaling pathway in physiology and pathology, our findings raise the likelihood of ARL15 as the causative gene and suggest the contribution of the TGFβ family signaling pathway to the pathology of these metabolic diseases.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this as a conclusion based on the findings.

claim: The expression level of ARL15 might vary in particular genetic background, therefore correspondingly changing the strength of the TGFβ family signaling.
source: We hypothesize that the expression level of ARL15 might vary in particular genetic background, therefore correspondingly changing the strength of the TGFβ family signaling.
evidence: The discussion explicitly states this as a hypothesis.
